description_good_justification: The README describes primitives for SSI libraries and applications: DIDs, key management behind a pluggable key store, and JWT-based verifiable credentials. It lists capabilities and Cargo features. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit#readme
interact_justification: Obtain: `cargo add identity-kit` from crates.io (https://crates.io/crates/identity-kit), as the README says. Feedback: bug reports and feature requests go to GitHub issues (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/issues), linked from the README's Development section. Contribute: CONTRIBUTING.md, also linked there.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md describes pull requests, squash merging, Conventional Commits titles and the development checks. The workflow files define which checks run for each event and changed path. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks: code must pass `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, the tests, rustdoc with `-D warnings`, `cargo hack` per feature, `cargo deny` and the layer-boundary build. It must respect the MSRV, and PR titles follow Conventional Commits.
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers features, Cargo features, key stores and how to extend the crate (new DID methods, key store backends). docs/DESIGN.md describes the architecture: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/docs/DESIGN.md
documentation_interface_justification: API documentation is published on docs.rs. Cargo.toml enables `missing_docs`, and CI runs rustdoc with `-D warnings` and doctests through `cargo test`. https://docs.rs/identity-kit
sites_https_justification: The project, package distribution and API documentation are available over HTTPS: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit, https://crates.io/crates/identity-kit and https://docs.rs/identity-kit.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests provide searchable discussions with URLs for topics and comments. Participation requires a GitHub account; the interface works in a web browser, including FLOSS browsers. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/issues
english_justification: The README, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md and API documentation are written in English. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit#readme
maintained_justification: The public history records ongoing development and maintenance, including v0.2.0 released on 2026-10-23 and the dependency advisory update in PR #95. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/releases/tag/v0.2.0 https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/95
repo_track_justification: Git records changes, commit authors and timestamps. Pull requests provide associated discussion and CI results. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/commits/main/
repo_interim_justification: The public repository exposes development commits and pull requests between tagged releases. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pulls
version_unique_justification: Each release has its own version (v0.0.2, v0.1.0, v0.2.0), published on crates.io, where versions can't be reused.
version_semver_justification: The release process follows Cargo SemVer rules and uses release-plz with Conventional Commits and `cargo-semver-checks`. The PR SemVer job compares the public API against the base commit unless the title already declares a breaking change with `!`, in which case the API check is skipped. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/qa.yml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/docs/RELEASE.md
version_tags_justification: Library releases such as v0.0.2, v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 have git tags and GitHub releases. The release workflow creates these when publishing. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/tags https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/docs/RELEASE.md
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md uses Keep a Changelog sections and marks breaking changes. The release workflow also publishes release notes on GitHub. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: SECURITY.md describes publishing GitHub and RustSec advisories after a fix. A maintainer still needs to confirm whether any release fixed a project vulnerability with an assigned identifier and, if so, whether its release notes identify it. Dependency advisories are outside this criterion. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/SECURITY.md
report_responses_justification: Public bug reports have been addressed in linked pull requests, for example #76 by #82, #77 by #83, #78 by #84 and #79 by #85. This does not assert that every open issue has been answered. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/issues/79 https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/85
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests have resulted in implementations, for example #53 in #74 and #61 in #64. Other requests remain open or are declined, such as #139, which has a response and a `wontfix` label. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/issues/53 https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/issues/61 https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/issues/139
report_archive_justification: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/issues?q=is%3Aissue (open and closed issues stay public and searchable).
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports go through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, which is enabled: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/security/advisories/new (described in SECURITY.md).
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging vulnerability reports within 14 days. Actual response history, including private reports, needs maintainer confirmation before this criterion can be answered. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_floss_tools_justification: The project builds with the FLOSS Rust toolchain. The License workflow checks dependency licenses against the FLOSS allow-list in deny.toml on PRs and main pushes that change Cargo manifests, Cargo.lock, deny.toml or that workflow. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/license.yml
test_justification: `cargo test --all-features` runs unit tests, integration tests and doctests. The suite includes specification vectors from W3C, IETF, DIF and DID method specifications, plus behavioral and regression tests. CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to run it; the repository is licensed Apache-2.0. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
test_most_justification: On 2026-11-02, `cargo llvm-cov --all-features` on main (4f95dbd) covered 95.86% of lines, 94.95% of regions and 93.55% of functions; Codecov reports 94.34% for the same code. Branch coverage is not measured, since it needs a nightly toolchain. The Coverage workflow measures every pull request, and a weekly cargo-mutants run reports missed mutants in an issue, none open on that date. https://codecov.io/gh/impierce/identity-kit https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/coverage.yml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutants.yml
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: QA runs tests on Linux, macOS and Windows, plus MSRV, clippy and documentation checks, on PRs and pushes to main. Dependency license and advisory checks have separate workflows filtered to Cargo manifests, Cargo.lock, deny.toml and their respective workflow files; advisory checks also run daily. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/qa.yml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/audit.yml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/license.yml
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests: a pull request that adds or changes functionality adds tests for it, and a bug fix adds a test that fails without the fix, using the specifications' own test vectors.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent major changes each came with tests: KeyReference and KeyResolver (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/74), refusing SD-JWT payloads in JWT validators (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/85, tests/vc_sd_jwt_payload.rs), the RSA 2048-bit minimum (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/83) and the SD-JWT nesting limit (https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/82).
warnings_justification: Cargo.toml forbids unsafe code and enables `missing_docs`, `unreachable_pub`, `missing_debug_implementations` and `clippy::pedantic`. `must_use_candidate` and `assert_is_empty` are explicitly disabled; documented `#[expect]` exceptions are used where appropriate. QA runs clippy with `-D warnings` for all targets with all features and for each feature separately, and rustdoc with `-D warnings`. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/Cargo.toml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/qa.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: The configured clippy and rustdoc checks fail on warnings because QA passes `-D warnings`. CONTRIBUTING.md requires these checks to pass. This describes the checks, not a guarantee that repository administrators cannot bypass them. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/qa.yml
warnings_strict_justification: CI treats enabled rustc, clippy and rustdoc warnings as errors. The lint baseline includes `clippy::pedantic`, with `must_use_candidate` and `assert_is_empty` disabled and documented `#[expect]` exceptions. Clippy also checks each feature separately. Project-authored Rust forbids unsafe code. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/Cargo.toml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/qa.yml
crypto_published_justification: The JOSE implementation supports Ed25519, ECDSA with P-256 and secp256k1, and RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS signatures with SHA-2, using published algorithms and the JOSE profiles in RFCs 7515, 7518 and 8037. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/src/jose/algorithm.rs
crypto_call_justification: Software signatures and hashes use ed25519-dalek, p256, k256, rsa and sha2 rather than project-authored primitives. Default software key generation and SD-JWT salts use getrandom. The PKCS#11 backend delegates key generation and signing to the configured module; the default HTTP client uses reqwest with rustls for TLS. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/Cargo.toml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/src/keys/pkcs11.rs
crypto_floss_justification: The software crypto and default TLS implementations are FLOSS dependencies; deny.toml lists the accepted licenses, including MIT, Apache-2.0 and ISC. The optional PKCS#11 backend can use the FLOSS SoftHSM2 module, which CI tests. Users may instead choose a proprietary token module. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/deny.toml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/qa.yml
crypto_keylength_justification: Software backends generate Ed25519, P-256 and, when enabled, secp256k1 keys. The PKCS#11 backend also supports RSA-2048 and RSA-4096 generation. JOSE RSA verification rejects moduli shorter than 2048 bits. These sizes meet this criterion's stated NIST minimums through 2030. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/src/keys/pkcs11.rs https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/pull/83
crypto_working_justification: The supported JOSE algorithms use Ed25519, ECDSA and RSA with SHA-2, not MD4, MD5, DES or RC4. The `none` JWS algorithm is rejected. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/src/jose/algorithm.rs
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The JOSE signing and verification profiles use SHA-2 rather than SHA-1. The documented rsa timing advisory is avoided in the RustCrypto dependency by restricting it to public-key operations; PKCS#11 private-key operations are delegated to the selected module. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/src/jose/algorithm.rs https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-rsa-verification-only.md
crypto_pfs_justification: The library implements no key-agreement protocol itself; HTTPS goes through the `HttpClient` the caller supplies. The default `ReqwestClient` uses rustls 0.23 with the ring provider, which offers only TLS 1.3 and ECDHE TLS 1.2 cipher suites, so every connection it makes has forward secrecy. An application that supplies its own client chooses its own TLS settings. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/Cargo.toml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/src/methods/web/client.rs
crypto_password_storage_justification: The library does not implement password authentication for external users or a password-verifier database. PKCS#11 PIN handling authenticates to a token, rather than authenticating external users to this library. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/src/keys/pkcs11.rs
crypto_random_justification: Default software key generation and the default SD-JWT salt generator use getrandom; salts contain 128 random bits and decoys hash generated salts. InMemoryKeyStore also offers deterministic fixture-only generation, and callers can supply salts. PKCS#11 key generation uses the selected module's generator. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/src/keys/in_memory.rs https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/src/sd_jwt_vc/builder.rs https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/src/keys/pkcs11.rs
delivery_mitm_justification: Crates are distributed through crates.io over HTTPS with registry checksums. From v0.2.0 onward, the release process attaches the crate and SLSA provenance generated through Sigstore; docs/RELEASE.md explains verification. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/releases/tag/v0.2.0 https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/docs/RELEASE.md
delivery_unsigned_justification: The release workflow downloads the crate and registry checksum over HTTPS and checks their match before attaching the artifact. The documented Cargo installation uses crates.io. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-plz.yml
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: The Audit workflow checks RustSec advisories on relevant dependency and configuration changes and daily. deny.toml and osv-scanner.toml document exceptions: RUSTSEC-2023-0071 because the RustCrypto rsa dependency is used only for public-key operations (PKCS#11 signing occurs in the module), and RUSTSEC-2026-0387 because the affected crypto-bigint 0.5.5 is used by the `rust_crypto` feature of the test-only jsonwebtoken dev-dependency. These checks and exceptions do not establish the complete vulnerability-remediation history; maintainer confirmation is needed. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/deny.toml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/audit.yml
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: SECURITY.md describes the vulnerability-reporting and fix-publication process. Whether all reported critical vulnerabilities have been fixed needs confirmation from maintainers with access to the complete report history. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/SECURITY.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: On 2026-11-02, the lines added by every commit on every branch (381 commits) were scanned for GitHub, AWS, Slack, Google, Stripe, crates.io, npm, OpenAI and Anthropic tokens, PEM private keys, credentials in URLs and credential assignments. The two matches were a test URL with placeholder credentials on example.com and a constant naming a test-vector file. The private keys in the repository are test keys only: published specification vectors such as RFC 8037 A.1 and RFC 8032 test 1, and synthetic keys, in tests, documentation examples and doctests. Release credentials are not in the repository: crates.io publishing uses OIDC trusted publishing, and the GitHub App private key is a GitHub Actions secret. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/tests/jose_jws.rs https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-plz.yml
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (Rust and GitHub Actions, `security-extended` queries) and clippy run on every pull request and every push to `main`: https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/actions/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's `security-extended` query suite looks for common vulnerabilities.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: On 2026-11-02, the GitHub code-scanning API returned no open alerts for the CodeQL tool. Other tools, including Scorecard, have separate findings; this is not a claim that the entire code-scanning dashboard is empty. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/security/code-scanning
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and push to `main`, and weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The Fuzz workflow discovers cargo-fuzz targets and runs each for 60 seconds on PRs matching its source, fuzz, Cargo or workflow path filters, and 600 seconds on nightly or manual runs. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Project-authored library code is Rust with `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. This does not assert that dependencies or external PKCS#11 modules contain no unsafe or native code. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/Cargo.toml
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz targets build with debug assertions and overflow checks (cargo-fuzz's default) and assert their own invariants, such as round-trips. The tests run with debug assertions on.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The Fuzz workflow retains crash artifacts on failure, and fuzz/run.sh includes committed seeds in subsequent runs. Whether all confirmed findings have been resolved needs a review of crash artifacts and triage history; the workflow alone does not establish it. https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/impierce/identity-kit/blob/main/fuzz/run.sh
